pointers.sentence: The model's `objects` is a manager the metaclass, `ModelBase`, added, because the class declared none (`django/db/models/base.py:ModelBase._prepare`).
So the view's `filter` is `get_queryset` followed by `QuerySet.filter` (`django/db/models/manager.py:BaseManager._get_queryset_methods`; [Managers](../models/managers.md)).
A new `QuerySet` holds a new `Query` for its model and the class that will turn rows into objects, `ModelIterable` (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.__init__`).
The `Query` is the ORM's description of a statement to be: the tables it joins, the conditions, the ordering, what to select (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query`).

`QuerySet.filter` clones the queryset it is called on, applies the filter to the clone, and returns the clone, so that a queryset can be kept and refined into several others (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet._filter_or_exclude`).

The clone has its own `Query`, which `Query.clone` makes by copying the mutable parts, the where clause among them (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.clone`) ([The query: what a `Query` holds, and how it is copied](../query/anatomy.md)).
The keyword arguments become a `Q`, an object holding conditions, which `&` and `|` combine (`django/db/models/query_utils.py:Q`).
The work is in `Query.build_filter`, which turns one `"published__year"` with its value into a condition (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.build_filter`) ([Building a query](../query.md)):

`Query.solve_lookup_type` splits the name at the double underscores: `"published"` is a field of the model, a `DateField`, not a relation, so `"year"` is left over (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.solve_lookup_type`, `django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.names_to_path`).

`Query.setup_joins` makes no join for `"published"`, and `build_filter` asks the field for its column, a `Col` (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.setup_joins`, `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.get_col`).

The transform's `"exact"` lookup is `YearExact`, a `YearLookup`, and it is made with the transform on its left and `2026` on its right (`django/db/models/lookups.py:YearExact`).

The rule is that the last name is a lookup if what it applies to has one so named, and otherwise a transform, with `"exact"` as the lookup (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.build_lookup`) ([Expressions, lookups and functions](../expressions.md)).
`QuerySet.order_by` clones and clears the ordering, and `Query.add_ordering` checks that `"published"` names a field and stores the name itself (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.add_ordering`).
It becomes a column only when the statement is compiled (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name`).

Each goes through `QuerySet._fetch_all`, which fills the result cache, if there is none yet, with the list its iterable class, `ModelIterable`, yields (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet._fetch_all`).

`ModelIterable.__iter__` then does the whole of one query: it asks the router which database to read from, asks the `Query` for a compiler for that database's backend, runs it, and turns each row into an instance (`django/db/models/query.py:ModelIterable.__iter__`).

It builds the clauses and joins them as `"SELECT"`, `"FROM"`, `"WHERE"`, `"ORDER BY"`, appending each clause's parameters in the same order, so that the placeholders and the parameters line up (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.as_sql`; [The compiler: `as_sql`, `execute_sql` and `results_iter`](../sql/compiler.md)).
Each node of the query writes its own SQL, and here `SQLCompiler.compile` calls a node's `as_sql` (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.compile`).
The where clause joins its children's SQL with `"AND"`, and its one child is the year lookup (`django/db/models/sql/where.py:WhereNode.as_sql`).

So the recorded statement's two parameters are the two dates (`django/db/models/lookups.py:YearLookup.as_sql`, `django/db/backends/base/operations.py:BaseDatabaseOperations.year_lookup_bounds_for_date_field`).

So the recorded statement's two parameters are the two dates (`django/db/models/lookups.py:YearLookup.as_sql`, `django/db/backends/base/operations.py:BaseDatabaseOperations.year_lookup_bounds_for_date_field`).
The statement needs a cursor, and `BaseDatabaseWrapper.cursor` opens the connection if there is none (`django/db/backends/base/base.py:BaseDatabaseWrapper.cursor`).

What `BaseDatabaseWrapper.connect` opens and `close` discards is the driver's connection inside it (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper`, `django/utils/connection.py:BaseConnectionHandler.__getitem__`).

What `BaseDatabaseWrapper.connect` opens and `close` discards is the driver's connection inside it (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper`, `django/utils/connection.py:BaseConnectionHandler.__getitem__`).

`connect` notes when that connection is to be closed, from the database's `"CONN_MAX_AGE"`, and then has the backend's `get_new_connection` open it (`django/db/backends/base/base.py:BaseDatabaseWrapper.connect`).

With `"AUTOCOMMIT"` true, the default, and `"ATOMIC_REQUESTS"` false, no transaction is opened around the query: each statement is a transaction of its own, which the database commits as it ends (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper._set_autocommit`; [Transactions: autocommit, `atomic` and savepoints](../connections/atomic.md)).

The driver's cursor is wrapped in a `CursorWrapper`, whose `execute` passes it the statement (`django/db/backends/utils.py:CursorWrapper.execute`; [Cursors: executing a statement, the query log and execute wrappers](../connections/cursors.md)).

`SQLCompiler.results_iter` returns a generator over the rows the cursor fetched, which applies the converters the backend declares for each column's type as `ModelIterable.__iter__` takes each row (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.results_iter`).

Here the column, declared `"date"`, was already parsed by a converter the backend registers with the driver, so the backend's finds a date and leaves it; a column with no declared type, such as a function's, would reach it as text (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/operations.py:DatabaseOperations.convert_datefield_value`, `django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py`; [Values in and out: adapters, converters and time zones](../backends/values.md)).

For each converted row `Model.from_db` makes the instance: it calls the class with the values in field order, then marks the instance as not being added and records the database it came from (`django/db/models/base.py:Model.from_db`).
